markers.reading: The party finishes a late breakfast after the morning gnoll fight and short rest.

evidence.quote: a group of adventurers is finishing a late breakfast.
As you eat and rest, small clues and hints of the mystery of this place drift across your minds.
As you finish your breakfast, Kenzo—or sorry, Wellby—looks up, having just completed his sketch of the ruins.
you fought the gnolls like first thing in the morning, then you short rested, and it's been a while exploring.

time.basis: Late breakfast is narrated; the date is not independently spoken.

markers.note: The later short-rest reference places a completed rest before exploration; its one-hour convention does not establish that the entire rest occurs after this transcript opens.

markers.reading: Delwath spends a few minutes examining the mists with fey sight while the others handle the items.

evidence.quote: Um, Tim? Yeah, I'm gonna kind of wander outside while they're doing this and more closely with my fey sight at the unexplored mists.
I will spend a few minutes.
There's a, there's a something from another, another world, some energy. It came it came to this earth from, from somewhere else. Sort of now in the valley, where the road crosses.

duration.basis: Declared investigation is followed by its narrated findings.

markers.reading: Riswynn spends about 10–15 minutes praying over each of the three newly identified items.

evidence.quote: Yeah, it takes like 10–15 minutes praying over each one to get a sense. Um.
Riswynn is just finishing identifying items with Vola standing by her.

duration.basis: DM gives the duration per item, not the aggregate duration.

markers.note: Overlaps the surrounding item conversation and split-party searching; do not add the conversation time again.

markers.reading: Seeker spends a minute estimating where the ley lines cross.

evidence.quote: They, if you—so Seeker spends a minute sort of concentrating and like doing a little bit of like trigonometry in his head. And, you know, based on the way that they're crossing here, you would think they would probably cross each other and create a node where the dwarven fort is.

duration.basis: DM explicitly narrates a minute of concentration.

markers.reading: Delwath briefly reads the hobgoblin logbook and scouting papers; the DM revises the initial fifteen-minute estimate to about ten minutes.

evidence.quote: spending 15 minutes kind of flipping through it
I mean, I'm only gonna spend a few minutes flipping...
Yeah, this is basically what you get into—in, like, 10 minutes kind of flipping through.

duration.basis: Later DM estimate corrects the initial fifteen minutes.

markers.reading: The bridge approach is in morning light, subsequently placed at about 10:30–11 and nearing noon.

evidence.quote: And that actually, in the morning light, is, you know the sun is catching it, looks quite pretty, this cascading silvery waterfall.
It's like 10:30, 11.
It's still morning. Man. You probably mean, that you fought the gnolls like first thing in the morning, then you short rested, and it's been a while exploring. Is probably just before lunchtime.
It's getting close towards noon, so there's there's not a ton of shadows.

markers.note: “Morning” is the table’s description; these clock values fall in the review’s midday watch (10–14).

time.basis: Narrated morning; the DM gives an uncertain 10:30–11 clock estimate, both within the review’s midday watch.

markers.reading: After the fight, Delwath and Seeker finish erasing the runes in less than roughly 15–20 seconds.

evidence.quote: Okay. Between you and you sort of slashing at them with your sword and Seeker erupting the earth around them, within a few, you know less than you know, 15–20 seconds, you've now sort of eliminated any sign that they were there. And the mists continue to blow away as you do this.

duration.basis: DM says less than 15–20 seconds; twenty seconds is one-third of a minute.

markers.reading: Delwath takes ten minutes to check the remaining magic, finding residue in the ash.

evidence.quote: Magic gone, the angry...? I mean, I'll take 10 minutes to...
Yes. Ah, so it is—yes, it is gone, except for—you see on the, on the ground, there is—you do sense that there is like a small residual magic left

duration.basis: Declared ten-minute examination is accepted and resolved by the DM.

markers.reading: The party returns through the secret exit to its horses in the afternoon.

evidence.quote: So as you head out quietly through the secret door, back down the passageway, Vola following silently behind, in the afternoon you return...
You come out through the clear water of the mountain stream protecting the back entrance to the dwarven hold, to your horses, the camp you had set up

markers.reading: The party rides south for a few hours and reaches a place to camp for the evening.

evidence.quote: And turn, riding south for a few hours to some place to camp for the evening. As we will end our session there.

yamlCheck.dateAnchor: The calendar date 1748-04-13 comes entirely from YAML. The transcript establishes morning, a near-noon bridge approach, afternoon return, and evening camp.
yamlCheck.explanation: Continuous same-day play ends at evening camp without an overnight. Yesterday’s demon fight, the earlier long rest, historical occupation dates, and Delwath’s backstory are recalled history. “At dawn tomorrow” is a proposed animal instruction; the accepted narration immediately sends the animals away (u2393–u2422), followed by the afternoon return.
